result.description: MYT Framing Solutions  MYT Framing Pty Ltd is seeking a full-time Production Operator to assist with the manufacturing and assembly of light gauge steel framing components for residential and commercial construction projects. The role involves operating production machinery, cutting, shaping, assembling and finishing steel framing components, monitoring equipment, conducting quality checks, maintaining safe work practices, and preparing completed products for dispatch.  The successful candidate will support the production of wall frames, roof trusses, floor joists and other structural steel components, ensuring all products are manufactured accurately, efficiently and in accordance with company standards and project specifications.   Benefits   Competitive salary package with Superannuation  Full time job opportunity and long term career prospects  Supportive, team based environment  Ongoing training and skill development opportunities  On site Parking  Task & Responsibilities  Operate production equipment in a safe and efficient manner.  Handle raw materials, including steel components.  Assist with the production, assembly and preparation of frames for construction projects.  Maintain a clean and safe work environment.  Follow work instructions and company safety policies.    Task & responsibilities   Operating specialised production machinery and equipment used for cutting, shaping, joining, assembling and finishing steel framing components.  Reading and following production sheets, technical specifications, drawings and work instructions to ensure accurate manufacturing of housing components.  Calibrating machinery, monitoring gauges and making necessary adjustments to maintain smooth and efficient production.  Conducting regular checks on machinery and equipment to ensure safe and effective operation.  Performing basic troubleshooting, minor repairs and adjustments to machinery where required.  Carrying out quality checks on finished components to ensure they meet company standards, project requirements and relevant construction specifications.  Identifying and reporting defects, production issues or equipment faults to supervisors in a timely manner.  Assisting with the packaging, labelling and preparation of completed framing components for dispatch to construction sites.  Checking and maintaining material inventory levels, including assisting with monthly stock counts and warehouse organisation.  Following workplace health and safety procedures, equipment manuals and company policies at all times.  Maintaining a clean, organised and safe production area to support efficient workflow and reduce downtime.  Working collaboratively with production, warehouse, logistics and site teams to ensure orders are completed accurately and delivered on schedule.    Qualification & experience  The successful candidate must have at least  2 year of relevant work experience  in a production, manufacturing, fabrication, construction, steel framing or similar industrial environment.   The candidate should be able to read and follow production sheets, technical drawings, equipment manuals and workplace safety instructions. They should have practical knowledge of machine operation, material handling, basic troubleshooting, quality checking and safe workplace practices.  Experience in light gauge steel framing, structural steel fabrication, warehouse operations, inventory control or dispatch preparation would be advantageous.   The candidate must demonstrate strong attention to detail, good teamwork skills, the ability to follow instructions, and a commitment to maintaining quality, safety and productivity standards.  About Company    MYT Framing Pty Ltd is a South Australian company specialising in light gauge steel framing and structural steel solutions for residential and commercial building projects. The company provides a complete service including drafting, engineering, fabrication, delivery and installation of steel framing components.  MYT Framing works with commercial builders, boutique home builders and property developers, offering reliable advice, precision fabrication and professional installation services. The company focuses on delivering high-quality, accurate and durable steel framing products while maintaining strong standards of safety, efficiency and workmanship. Job description:

 
Department of Health seeks an IT Officer - Network Communications to support network, Wi-Fi, communications and connectivity services.

 

 






 

The Team

Digital Infrastructure Services provides the foundational technology platforms that keep Tasmania's public health system connected, secure and operational. The team delivers and supports enterprise data centres, compute and storage platforms, virtualisation, data protection, network connectivity, Wi-Fi and core infrastructure services that underpin clinical, corporate and business systems across the state.

Working in a complex 24 7 always-on health environment, the team plays a critical role in service reliability, cyber resilience, asset lifecycle management, infrastructure modernisation, and the delivery of technology that directly supports frontline care. This is your opportunity to join a high-performing team delivering Digital Infrastructure services to hospitals, health facilities, clinicians, staff and the Tasmanian community.

The Role

Join Digital Infrastructure Services and help support the network and communications services that keep Tasmania's public health system connected, secure and operational.

In this entry-level role, you will assist with the day-to-day support of enterprise network, communications, Wi-Fi and connectivity services across a large 24 7 health environment. Working with an experienced team, you will support incidents and service requests, assist with troubleshooting, maintain documentation, liaise with stakeholders, and coordinate with vendors and service providers.

This is a great opportunity for someone early in their ICT career to build practical experience in enterprise networking and communications while contributing to services that directly support hospitals, clinicians, staff and the Tasmanian community.

You will need

A sound foundation in IT and networking concepts, with an interest in communications, connectivity and infrastructure support.

The ability to support service delivery, including troubleshooting issues, assisting with incidents and service requests, and working effectively with team members, vendors and service providers.

Strong communication, teamwork and organisational skills, with the ability to follow documented processes and work effectively in a busy environment with competing priorities.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     EAST COAST MEDICAL NETWORK - AMR 2027

Applications Close: Tuesday, 4th August 2026, 11:59pm AEST.

 

The East Coast Medical Network may offer 1 or 2 year contracts (as required for completion of basic training) to applicants who have completed their time in an accredited Basic Physician Trainee (BPT) role. All other applicants will be offered 3-year contracts, subject to change, with final rankings from the application process and service provision requirements determining the length of training contract that will be offered. 

 

Previous or current registration with RACP in non-BPT roles does not guarantee a 2-year contract.

Please also note that once a BPT offer is accepted, any application you make for any subsequent round BPT position during the 2027 AMR campaign will not be considered whilst you are holding that offer.

Employment Type: Temporary Full-Time
Remuneration: As per Award
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM29193

An exciting opportunity exists to join the East Coast Medical Network as a Basic Physician Trainee. 

Where you'll be working

 

The East Coast Medical Network is dedicated to training balanced, well-rounded and competent physicians.

Vocationally based training is delivered across five locations along the spectacular East Coast of New South Wales: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sydney Hospital, The Royal Hospital for Women, Port Macquarie Base Hospital and Shellharbour Hospital.

We support our trainees to reach their full potential through an interactive and individualised education program underpinned by the principles of opportunity, equity and fairness. While the success of the network is reflected in our consistently strong performance in the RACP written and clinical examinations, we measure success more broadly through the ability of our graduates to secure their preferred advanced training positions and through the strong reputation ECMN trainees for their knowledge, clinical acumen and work ethic.

The ECMN offers a broad range of subspecialty medical terms across both metropolitan and regional settings. There are no standalone night terms within the network. A comprehensive preference system is used to allocate rotations and annual leave, with the aim of providing trainees with a diverse range of clinical experiences.

Our written education program complements the RACP's Physician Education Program and is delivered weekly during protected teaching time. Sessions focus on direct interaction with experts in their fields and are video conferenced to all peripheral sites from the first week of training. All trainees are given the opportunity to attend a two-week revision course in the penultimate year of their ECMN training contract, regardless of the duration of prior RACP training completed.

Our clinical examination preparation program is comprehensive and includes several structured activities each week, including practice short and long cases, dedicated neurology teaching and communication skills tutorials. Trainees are eligible to participate in the clinical examination preparation program during the final year of their ECMN training contract, regardless of the duration of prior training completed.

Our professional development program aims to broaden trainees' skills beyond clinical medicine, with sessions covering leadership, supervision of junior medical officers, communication, curriculum vitae preparation and interview skills. There are also significant opportunities to become involved in teaching and research through the network's strong affiliation with the University of New South Wales.

More information about the ECMN can be found on our website.

What you'll be doing 

The primary purpose of the Basic Physician Trainee (BPT) is to provide effective medical services to patients under supervision, while developing expertise in medical practice in a complex clinical environment in inpatient and outpatient areas in the public health organisations within the Network. 

Basic Physician Training roles consist of rotations through medical departments, working under an appropriate level of supervision by consultants. Rotations have different levels of responsibility and team structures. BPTs will gain increasing clinical autonomy and accountability as team leaders throughout the course of the training program, building on their skills and attributes with the goal of entering an Advanced Training program. 

BPTs undertaking the care of medical patients should ensure that they operate within their own level of expertise within a collaborative clinical care model and seek consultation with the treating physician when appropriate, in the following activities: 
 

Clinically assess patients, incorporating consultation-history taking, examination, and formulation of a differential diagnosis and management plans

Discuss diagnoses and management plans with patients and their families or carers

Document the progress of patients in multiple settings

Prescribe medications tailored to patients' needs and conditions

Transfer care of patients

Choose, organise and interpret investigations

Assess and manage acutely unwell patients

Plan, prepare for, perform, and provide after care for important procedures 

 

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS:
 

MBBS or equivalent, current general registration with the Medical Board of Australia.

If the applicant's registration has conditions, all conditions will be assessed by the health agency to determine if the applicant can meet the essential requirements of the role.

A minimum of three (3) years post- graduate experience or two (2) full years of postgraduate experience in public hospital service by the start of the clinical year.

Eligible for or holding current registration as a Basic Physician Trainee with the Royal Australasian College of Physicians and intent to obtain Fellowship of Royal Australasian College of Physicians.

ALS certification or equivalent by the start of the clinical year.

Valid Working with Children check

Cleared National Police Check

To be employed by NSW Health you are required to provide evidence of vaccination to comply with the NSW Health Occupational Assessment, Screening & Vaccination against Specified Infectious Diseases Policy, this includes any amendments made from time to time.
